name: BTC social-attention contagion — buy the alt the day after BTC's crowd spikes
rationale: NON-OBVIOUS finding from the cross-asset contagion study in the probe: a spike in BITCOIN's social_volume (BTC social acceleration, ln v_t/v_{t-1}) LEADS the mean-ALT forward return — corr(BTC social-change_t, mean-ALT fwd return) = +0.068 at k=1, +0.064 at k=2, decaying to +0.027 by k=3 (n~1000 days). A head-to-head OLS confirms it is BTC's CROWD, not its price: standardized beta on BTC_social_accel +0.064 (t=+2.01) dominates BTC_price_return -0.016 (t=-0.50). The lead is the SAME sign and shape as the within-asset attention-acceleration effect, but it is BTC's crowd read on the ALTS — when attention floods into Bitcoin, the alt complex pops the next 1-2 days. The failed cross-asset-social-rotation spec rotated on each asset's OWN social VOLUME LEVEL (always-true on the 160x-drifted scale) and never tested a cross-asset lead at all. This spec enters a long in an alt the day AFTER btc_social_accel clears a floor (BTC attention spiked, known next day — point-in-time), while the alt itself is not already crowded (own social_attention_z below a ceiling) and not falling, and holds 1-2 days (the contagion is gone by k=3). Disconfirmer: the contagion is distinct ONLY if BTC's social lead beats the asset's OWN social lead AND beats BTC's PRICE lead. It is FALSIFIED if replacing btc_social_accel with the asset's own social_volume_accel (the Spec-1 trigger) does as well — then this is just the within-asset attention effect, not contagion. It is also FALSIFIED if a plain 'buy alts after BTC price rose' rule (BTC return contagion) does as well — then the social data adds nothing over price (this second leg is checked in the cohort harness/report, not encodable in the spec DSL). tier1 + low-confidence until validated OOS.
catalyst: Bitcoin social attention spikes; the alt complex follows 1-2 days later
